text:
Alyssa: quick sync recap from today's kernel working group — we hit a perf cliff when switching long-seq attention to the Triton path for batch sizes > 8 on A10s. looking for agreement on next steps.
Matt: saw that in the traces too. the KV cache spills look like the culprit, memory allocate pattern is different between Triton and CUTLASS paths.
Sanjay: data point: Triton kernels had ~12% better small-batch latency but regressed p95 at larger batches by ~40%.
Dina: i can reproduce with the eval harness — running `./bench/attn --model gpt-3-like --seq 2048 --batch 16` shows OOM-ish pauses, logs attached.
Kevin: attaching quick flame: Triton launches multiple small kernels that hammer the cudaMalloc pool; CUTLASS uses preallocated workspace in our wrapper.
Elaine: can we summarize this as two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel memory allocation / workspace management, (2) attention algorithmic differences (tiling/fusion) causing different perf curves? :thinking_face:
Alyssa: exactly. proposed triage:
- short-term: revert Triton auto-select for long sequences on Dedicated A10s and fallback to CUTLASS path if batch >= 8 or seq >= 1024
- medium: add preallocated workspace API in runtime and enforce for Triton kernels
- long-term: converge on a common Kernel ABI for workspace + fused-ops to allow swap-in without allocation surprises
Matt: +1 for the revert/canary. can we gate behind a feature flag so hosted jobs can experiment?
Sanjay: feature-flag + telemetry is essential. need to collect: latency histograms, OOMs, and time-in-allocator.
Dina: created a quick patch branch with the fallback @matt — PR in draft: https://git.company/redwood/rt-inference/pull/4532
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary env(s) available: canary-a10-us-east-1, canary-a100-us-east-1
Kevin: dev note — implementing preallocated workspace is ~2 files: runtime/workspace.h + runtime/workspace_pool.cc and then a tiny kernel launch change. will prototype today.
Elaine: tricky part is cross-backend semantics: Triton kernels expect dynamic shapes and sometimes allocate internally. we need a clear contract: runtime MUST supply a pointer and size; kernel MUST not call cudamalloc. that'll make CUTLASS and Triton consistent.
Alyssa: agreed on contract. Sanjay / Kevin — can you draft a 1-pager RFC for the Kernel Workspace ABI? include: pointer lifetime, alignment, fallback behavior, pinned vs pageable memory.
Sanjay: will do. target EOD Friday for a first draft.
Matt: test plan requests:
- microbench: varying batch (1-32) and seq (128-4096) on A10/A100
- integration: full kv-cache replay for 2M tokens across shards
- regression detection: perf-alert if median latency regresses > 10% or p95 > 20% for a week
Dina: i'll add the microbench jobs to CI. estimate 3-4 hours to run full matrix, we should throttle nightly.
Kevin: note on CUTLASS: we still need to maintain a smaller set of tuned kernels for older nvidia drivers. Triton gives more flexibility but our runtime has to give it memory guarantees.
Elaine: also consider quantized kernels — int8 paths have different workspace needs. RFC should call out quantization variants.
Alyssa: good catch. add a section for quantized kernels and mixed-precision heuristics.
Sanjay: action items summary (adding owners):
- RFC: Kernel Workspace ABI (owner: Sanjay) — draft by Fri
- Runtime workspace pool + API (owner: Kevin) — prototype today / PR next week
- Canary rollout flag + telemetry (owner: Matt) — feature flag + metrics by Wed
- CI microbench matrix (owner: Dina) — jobs added, start nightly runs
- Perf alert thresholds and baseline (owner: Alyssa) — define by Tues
Matt: i'll wire the feature flag to the routes and make sure hosted customers get opt-in toggles.
Dina: small follow-up: bench script uses `--warmup 50 --iter 200`, should we increase warmup for Triton to account for JIT compile?
Kevin: yes, Triton needs longer warmup. set `--warmup 200` for Triton runs only.
Alyssa: timeline: short-term revert/canary by tomorrow AM; medium-term workspace API + canary enforcement next week; RFC + long-term ABI in 2 weeks.
Elaine: one more thing — user-visible policy: if we fallback to CUTLASS we should annotate traces and add routing hint so support can explain behavior to customers.
Sanjay: adding `kernel.variant` tag to traces (values: triton, cutlass, fallback) in today's PR.
Matt: :thumbsup: anyone opposed to the plan? otherwise i'll merge the canary flag PR after Dina's CI checks.
Kevin: no objections. will push workspace prototype branch soon.
Dina: CI job queued. will post links once results are in.
Alyssa: thanks team. i'll capture these action items in the sync notes and ping sales/support about the possible customer-visible fallback.
InfraBot: incident-bot: note created: KERNEL-REG-2026-03-20, priority P3, assignees: @Sanjay @Kevin
Matt: thanks — moving to follow-ups in #eng-runtime too.
Elaine: i'll add a short blurb to the architecture docs about the ABI goal so new contributors understand the constraint.
Alyssa: end of thread — see you in the kernel WG next week. :rocket:
